correctness.rationale: The source theorem gives Hurwitz degree 2p+2g-2 for smooth projective varieties. For the Segre product, the projective degree is the coefficient of A^a B^b in (A+B)^(a+b), and adjunction gives the sectional genus from K=-(a+1)A-(b+1)B. Substitution simplifies exactly to H=(2ab/(a+b))C. Reducing this rational multiplier proves the gcd formula. The coprimality classification then follows by an explicit computation for a=1 and the bound C>=binom(d,2)>d for a,b>=2. The bundled exact checker verifies all formulas for 1<=a,b<=200 without serving as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source proves the general Hurwitz-degree theorem and places the Hurwitz form next to the Chow form among higher associated hypersurfaces. It does not state the Segre-family gcd or classify when these two degrees are coprime. Targeted semantic and web searches using Segre, Chow, Hurwitz, gcd, common divisor, coprime, and associated-hypersurface formulations found no equivalent statement. Nearby results concern either Pluecker Grassmannians, full Segre coisotropic-degree gcds in a special 3-by-(n+1) family, or Segre-Veronese dual degrees, none of which implies this exact two-degree gcd formula.

value.rationale: The Chow and Hurwitz forms are consecutive canonical associated hypersurfaces attached to the same projective variety, encoding generic incidence and first-order nontransversality respectively. Their Pluecker degrees are therefore natural paired enumerative invariants. The exact gcd measures the universal arithmetic factor shared by those two incidence counts, and the theorem completely classifies the primitive cases across the entire two-parameter Segre family. The result distinguishes exactly the scrolls P^1 x P^{2m}, rather than an arbitrary finite or congruence slice.
